output_json.diff_review: patch_only.diff changes two files: (1) src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/util/StringUtils.java — replaces the unconditional pre-quoted shortcut (`source.startsWith(q) && source.endsWith(q)` → return verbatim) with a delimiter-aware guard that, for the single-quote delimiter, additionally requires the interior contain no single quote (source.indexOf('\'',1) == length-1). Malicious args with interior quotes now fall through to escape()+wrap. Behavior for non-single-quote delimiters (e.g. double-quote executable paths from unifyQuotes) is preserved, avoiding double-quoting regressions. (2) StringUtilsTest.java — adds testQuote_EscapeBrokenPreQuotedArgument asserting the breakout input is fully escaped, not returned verbatim. The change only tightens escaping; it never loosens it. pov.diff only adds new files under .security-pipeline/pov and is not touched by the fix, so the POV is unmodified. This is an appropriate minimal vulnerability fix at the correct sink in the taint trace.
issues: Minor/out-of-scope: for the double-quote delimiter the pre-quoted shortcut still trusts tokens verbatim, so $/backtick inside a double-quoted executable path are not neutralized. This is pre-existing behavior for internally-generated executable paths and outside the scope of this argument-injection finding; not a blocker.
output_json.pov_result: Reran `bash .security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh` via the Docker wrapper: shell argv now renders the tainted arg as fully escaped `echo ''\''a'\'' ; touch /tmp/plexus_pov_injected_marker ; '\''b'\'''`, marker file exists=false, RESULT: NOT VULNERABLE, POV_EXIT=1. Confirms the injection is neutralized (before-patch reference run was exit 0 / VULNERABLE with marker created).
output_json.regression_result: Reran `mvn -B -Dtest=StringUtilsTest,CommandlineTest,BourneShellTest test` via the Docker wrapper: 50 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS. Orchestrator's full `mvn -B test` run also passed (284 tests, 0 failures/0 errors). No regressions.
output_json.summary: The patch hardens StringUtils.quoteAndEscape() so an already-single-quoted argument containing interior single quotes is no longer trusted verbatim but fully escaped, closing the CWE-078 OS command injection in the Commandline/Shell rendering path. The POV no longer reproduces (exit 1, no marker file created) and all regression tests pass. The fix is minimal, targets the actual taint sink, does not modify or disable the POV, and removes no legitimate functionality.
